description: Quanta Buddies is a team of five young innovators from Bangladesh, united by a passion for space exploration, science, and technology. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we developed an interactive Martian exploration platform that brings together planetary mapping, terrain analysis, mission planning, environmental intelligence, and AI-powered assistance. Our goal is to make complex Mars data more accessible and support smarter, more informed planetary exploration.
summary:
Interplanetary Survival Guide Martain Map is an interactive, AI-assisted Martian exploration platform designed to make complex planetary data more accessible and useful for mission planning and exploration.

We developed an integrated system featuring four core components: Geo-Exploration, Mission Planning, Mission Intelligence, and Mission Response & Discovery. It brings together interactive 2D and 3D Martian mapping, terrain and elevation analysis, route planning, potential hazard assessment, environmental monitoring, and mission-support tools. Our AI-powered voice assistant, MARSIS, provides a conversational interface for exploring mission information and accessing AI-assisted insights.

The platform addresses the challenge of understanding and navigating an unfamiliar planetary environment by connecting different exploration tools and data sources in one workspace. Instead of treating planetary information as isolated datasets, it helps users interpret geographical and environmental information in the context of exploration decisions.

We aim to support mission planners, researchers, and future planetary explorers with a more accessible and integrated approach to understanding Mars.
details:
Interplanetary Survival Guide Martian Map

Project Overview

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is an AI-assisted planetary exploration and EVA (Extra-Vehicular Activity) mission-planning platform designed to help users understand Martian geography, evaluate terrain, and explore potential mission routes through an integrated interactive environment.

Exploring Mars presents major challenges: unfamiliar terrain, complex scientific datasets, potential surface hazards, and communication delays between Earth and Mars. Our project addresses these challenges by bringing geographical exploration, route planning, mission intelligence, and AI-assisted decision support together in one platform.

Four Core Systems

1. Geo-Exploration System — How can we turn an unknown planet into a world we can understand?

Provides interactive 2D and 3D Martian maps, regional exploration, elevation visualization, and terrain analysis. It helps users examine geographical features and better understand the Martian surface.

2. Mission Planning System — How do we find a suitable path through the uncharted?

Uses A* pathfinding, waypoint-based planning, elevation information, and slope analysis to evaluate possible routes. It helps users compare route options and identify terrain-related challenges during mission planning.

3. Mission Intelligence System — What is Mars telling us before conditions change?

Brings together relevant planetary datasets, environmental information, scientific observations, and mission-related information. It helps users interpret available evidence in the context of exploration decisions.

4. Mission Response & Discovery System — When the unexpected strikes, what’s our next move?

Provides access to potential hazard information, scientific target discovery, and mission-support insights. It helps users examine possible challenges and consider alternative exploration decisions.

AERIS — AI-Powered Voice Assistant

AERIS is our conversational AI assistant, powered by Google's Gemini technology. Users can ask questions about Martian geography, terrain, mission information, and route analysis through a natural-language interface. It makes the platform easier to interact with and provides AI-assisted explanations of available information.

How Does It Work?

The platform combines planetary mapping, scientific data, geospatial calculations, and AI-assisted interpretation.

  • Planetary imagery and topographic resources provide geographical context.
  • Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data supports elevation and terrain analysis.
  • Slope analysis helps identify potentially challenging terrain.
  • A* pathfinding calculates candidate routes based on the platform's available terrain information.
  • Waypoints allow users to organize and plan exploration paths.
  • The AI assistant helps explain information and respond to user queries.

Importantly, route calculations and terrain analysis are handled by computational methods, while AI is used to support explanations and interpretation. AI-generated suggestions are not treated as certified safety decisions.

Key Features

  1. Interactive 2D Mars Map
  2. CesiumJS-Based 3D Planetary Visualization
  3. Exploration of Major Martian Regions
  4. DEM-Based Elevation and Terrain Analysis
  5. A* Intelligent Route Calculation
  6. Waypoint-Based Mission Planning
  7. Terrain Slope and Potential Hazard Evaluation
  8. EVA Distance and Energy Estimation
  9. NASA MOLA Topographic Data Integration
  10. HiRISE and CTX Imagery Integration
  11. CRISM Mineralogical Data Integration
  12. Environmental Information and Mission Data Context
  13. Geographical Hazard Information
  14. Scientific Target Discovery
  15. Earth–Mars Communication Delay Simulation
  16. AI-Assisted Mission Explanations and Voice Interaction

Note: Keep each feature and dataset in this list only if it is implemented or genuinely integrated in your submitted version.

Tools and Technologies

  • Programming: TypeScript, JavaScript
  • Frontend: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS
  • Mapping and Visualization: CesiumJS, 2D Canvas
  • Geospatial Processing: DEM interpolation, slope-gradient analysis, Sobel-based image processing
  • Pathfinding: A* algorithm
  • Artificial Intelligence: Google Gemini API and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
  • Development Tools: Node.js, npm, Git, GitHub, Google AI Studio
  • Data Resources: NASA planetary science datasets and relevant Planetary Data System resources

Benefits and Intended Impact

The platform aims to make complex planetary information more accessible by connecting geographical data with practical exploration tools. It can support students, researchers, educators, and planetary mission-planning enthusiasts in understanding Martian terrain and evaluating potential exploration scenarios.

By combining mapping, terrain analysis, route planning, and AI-assisted explanations, the project offers a more integrated approach to exploring the challenges of operating on another planet.

Creativity and Design Considerations

Our project's creativity lies in combining several traditionally separate exploration functions into one interactive environment. Rather than simply displaying Martian maps, it connects terrain information with route evaluation, mission planning, scientific discovery, and conversational AI.

During development, we considered terrain complexity, data availability and resolution, computational limitations, communication delays, accessibility, and the distinction between calculated results and AI-generated explanations. We also considered how the platform could remain useful as a learning and planning tool without presenting simulated results as real-world mission guarantees.

Our vision is not simply to display Mars, but to help humanity understand its terrain, evaluate exploration possibilities, and prepare for the challenges of exploring another world.
